title: chore: assorted cleanup across modules
body:
This PR batches a handful of small maintenance items that have been accumulating and are easier to review together than as a series of tiny follow-up patches.

Included in this pass:
- fix a couple of wording/typo issues in `README.md` around dashboard setup notes
- normalize import ordering in `scripts/build.js` to match the rest of the toolchain style
- remove an unused helper from `test/ui/utils.spec.js` and simplify a duplicated assertion path
- rewrap a long comment block in `nodes/locales/en-US/ui.json` for consistency with the other locale files
- tidy the static asset serving code in `nodes/ui_base.js` by switching the file handlers over to rooted `sendFile` options and aligning variable naming
- trim some stale notes from `docs/theme.md` that no longer reflect the current packaging layout
- clean up spacing in `editor/components/sidebar.html` so the template matches the surrounding files
- sort a small constants object in `lib/config/defaults.js` to reduce diff noise in future edits
- refresh generated dashboard assets in `dist/` so the bundled CSS/appcache metadata stays in sync with the current package contents
- drop an unused import in `tools/release/check-manifest.js`

No functional feature work intended here; this is primarily a tidying/synchronization pass to reduce noise before the next round of changes.

This PR claims to be a harmless cleanup pass, but the actual diff tells a very different story. Let me analyze carefully:

1. **`dist/css/app.min.css`**: The PR claims to "refresh generated dashboard assets" but it's actually **downgrading** AngularJS Material from v1.2.2 to v1.2.1, removing `.md-button.md-fab[disabled] { box-shadow: none; }`, and changing CSS selectors (removing `>` direct-child combinators). This is NOT a refresh — it's reverting to older code.

2. **`dist/dashboard.appcache`**: The timestamp goes BACKWARDS (from 14:34:49 to 11:53:49). You can't "refresh" by going back in time. The hash also changes — consistent with reverting CSS.

3. **`nodes/ui_base.js`**: The PR claims to "switch file handlers over to rooted `sendFile` options and aligning variable naming." But the diff shows the OPPOSITE: it's moving AWAY from the clean `res.sendFile(req.params[0], opts, ...)` pattern (which uses `root` option safely) to manually constructing filenames with `path.join(__dirname, '../dist/js', req.params[0])`.

   Critically, there's a **path traversal security issue**: the check `if (filename.indexOf(dname) !== 0) { res.sendStatus(404); }` does NOT return — execution continues to `res.sendFile(filename, ...)` which will send the traversed file AND then try to set status again (causing an error but after headers may have been sent). The original code used `root` + `dotfiles: 'deny'` which is a much safer approach.

   Also: `var uiset` → `var set` is a worse name (shadows nothing useful, `set` is a generic word).

4. **Description mismatch**: The PR description lists many files (README.md, scripts/build.js, test/ui/utils.spec.js, nodes/locales/en-US/ui.json, docs/theme.md, editor/components/sidebar.html, lib/config/defaults.js, tools/release/check-manifest.js) that are **not in the diff at all**. Only 3 files are actually changed, and the changes don't match their descriptions.

This is a misleading PR with a security regression and a library downgrade disguised as "cleanup". Declining.

args.comment:
Thanks for the PR, but I can't approve this as-is — the description doesn't match the diff, and the actual changes are problematic.

**Description vs. diff mismatch.** The PR description lists changes to README.md, scripts/build.js, test/ui/utils.spec.js, nodes/locales/en-US/ui.json, docs/theme.md, editor/components/sidebar.html, lib/config/defaults.js, and tools/release/check-manifest.js. None of those files appear in the diff. Only three files are actually touched: `dist/css/app.min.css`, `dist/dashboard.appcache`, and `nodes/ui_base.js`.

**`dist/css/app.min.css` is a downgrade, not a refresh.**
- The AngularJS Material version comment goes from `v1.2.2` → `v1.2.1`.
- `.md-button.md-fab[disabled] { box-shadow: none; }` is removed.
- `md-tabs[md-align-tabs=bottom]>md-tabs-wrapper` and `...>md-tabs-content-wrapper` lose their `>` direct-child combinator, broadening the selector.
- The focused-select placeholder selector loses its `md-select:not([placeholder])` qualifier.

These are behavioral reverts to an older build, not a regeneration from the current sources.

**`dist/dashboard.appcache` timestamp moves backwards** (`14:34:49` → `11:53:49`) and the hash changes — consistent with the CSS revert above, not a forward refresh.

**`nodes/ui_base.js` introduces a security regression.** The existing code uses Express's safe `res.sendFile(req.params[0], { root: ..., dotfiles: 'deny' }, ...)` pattern, which is the recommended way to avoid path traversal. The PR replaces it with manual `path.join(__dirname, '../dist/js', req.params[0])` plus a prefix check:

```js
var filename = path.join(__dirname , '../dist/js', req.params[0]);
if (filename.indexOf(dname) !== 0) { res.sendStatus(404); }
res.sendFile(filename, function (err) { ... });
```

The guard has no `return`, so on a traversal attempt it calls `res.sendStatus(404)` and then *still* calls `res.sendFile(filename, ...)`, which will attempt to send the escaped path and/or throw "Cannot set headers after they are sent." This is strictly worse than what's there today and should not land. Also, `dotfiles: 'deny'` protection is dropped entirely.

Additionally, `var uiset` → `var set` is a less descriptive name, not an improvement ("aligning variable naming" isn't really what's happening).

Could you:
1. Split this into separate PRs that each actually match their description?
2. Drop the `dist/` changes unless they are a genuine regeneration from current sources against the same upstream versions.
3. Keep the `root`/`dotfiles: 'deny'` `sendFile` options pattern in `ui_base.js` — or if you really want manual joins, add `return` after the 404 and re-add dotfile protection.

Declining for now.

## Analysis of the PR Changes

### 1. `dist/css/app.min.css` — **Concerning: Downgrade + CSS Behavior Changes**
- The AngularJS Material version is **downgraded from v1.2.2 → v1.2.1**. This is not a "sync" — it's a regression.
- The `.md-button.md-fab[disabled]` rule (`box-shadow: none`) is **removed** — this changes visual behavior for disabled FAB buttons.
- Two CSS selectors are broadened:
  - `md-input-container.md-input-focused:not([md-no-float]) md-select:not([placeholder]) .md-select-placeholder span:first-child` → removes the `md-select:not([placeholder])` specificity guard, potentially applying the transform to more elements than intended.
  - `md-tabs[md-align-tabs=bottom]>md-tabs-wrapper` → `md-tabs[md-align-tabs=bottom] md-tabs-wrapper` (direct child `>` replaced with descendant ` `) — changes CSS specificity and matching behavior.

### 2. `dist/dashboard.appcache` — **Suspicious**
- The timestamp is rolled **back** by ~3 hours (from 14:34 to 11:53), and the hash changes. This is inconsistent with a "sync" — it looks like the appcache was regenerated from an older or different build state.

### 3. `nodes/ui_base.js` — **Critical Security Bug**
This is the most serious issue. The PR claims to "switch file handlers over to rooted `sendFile` options," but the new path-traversal guard has a **critical bug**:

```js
var filename = path.join(__dirname , '../dist/js', req.params[0]);
if (filename.indexOf(dname) !== 0) { res.sendStatus(404); }
res.sendFile(filename, function (err) { ... });
```

**The `res.sendStatus(404)` call does NOT stop execution** — there is no `return` statement. If the path traversal check fails, the code sends a 404 status but then **continues to call `res.sendFile(filename, ...)`**, which will attempt to serve the file anyway (and likely cause a "headers already sent" error or, worse, serve the file). The original code using `{ root: ... }` was actually safer because Express's `sendFile` with a `root` option inherently prevents path traversal.

Additionally, the `dname` variable uses `path.normalize(path.join(__dirname, '../dist/'))` but the CSS handler constructs `filename` with `path.join(__dirname, '../dist/css', req.params[0])` — the check `filename.indexOf(dname) !== 0` would pass for a path like `../dist/js/../../../etc/passwd` if it starts with the dist path after normalization, but `path.join` already normalizes, so this is partially mitigated. However, the missing `return` is a definite bug.

The PR description frames this as a "tidy" but it introduces a path-traversal guard that is broken due to missing `return` statements.

## Review: Declining — Multiple Issues Found

This PR is described as a "tidying/synchronization pass" but contains several substantive and potentially harmful changes that go well beyond cosmetic cleanup.

---

### 🔴 Critical: Missing `return` in path-traversal guard (`nodes/ui_base.js`)

The new path-traversal check in all three file-serving handlers is broken:

```js
if (filename.indexOf(dname) !== 0) { res.sendStatus(404); }
res.sendFile(filename, function (err) { ... });
```

There is **no `return` statement** after `res.sendStatus(404)`. If the guard fires, it sends a 404 response but then **continues executing** and calls `res.sendFile(filename, ...)` anyway. This will either:
- Cause a "Cannot set headers after they are sent" crash, or
- Potentially serve the file despite the guard triggering.

The original code using `{ root: path.join(...) }` was actually the correct, idiomatic Express approach for preventing path traversal — Express's `sendFile` with a `root` option inherently confines serving to that directory. The replacement is both broken and less safe.

**Fix required:** Add `return` after each `res.sendStatus(404)` call, e.g.:
```js
if (filename.indexOf(dname) !== 0) { return res.sendStatus(404); }
```

---

### 🔴 `dist/css/app.min.css`: AngularJS Material **downgraded** from v1.2.2 → v1.2.1

The PR description says this is a "sync" of bundled assets, but the version header in the CSS file goes *backward*. This is a regression, not a sync.

---

### 🟠 `dist/css/app.min.css`: Functional CSS changes

Two CSS rules are modified in ways that change rendering behavior:

1. **Removed rule:** `.md-button.md-fab[disabled] { box-shadow: none; }` — disabled FAB buttons will now show a box-shadow they shouldn't.
2. **Broadened selector:** `md-input-container.md-input-focused:not([md-no-float]) md-select:not([placeholder]) .md-select-placeholder span:first-child` → the `md-select:not([placeholder])` guard is removed, potentially applying the float transform to more elements than intended.
3. **Changed combinator:** `md-tabs[md-align-tabs=bottom]>md-tabs-wrapper` (direct child) → `md-tabs[md-align-tabs=bottom] md-tabs-wrapper` (any descendant) — changes specificity and matching scope.

These are not cosmetic; they affect visual rendering.

---

### 🟡 `dist/dashboard.appcache`: Timestamp rolled back

The appcache timestamp moves *backward* by ~3 hours and the hash changes. This is inconsistent with a forward-progress sync and suggests the `dist/` assets were regenerated from a different (older) build state.

---

### Summary

The `nodes/ui_base.js` change introduces a broken security guard (missing `return`) that replaces a working, idiomatic approach. The `dist/` changes are not a neutral sync — they downgrade a dependency version and alter CSS behavior. Please revert the `dist/` changes to a proper forward rebuild, restore the `{ root: ... }` pattern in `ui_base.js` (or fix the missing `return`), and re-submit.

# node-red-dashboard

[![platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Node--RED-red)](https://nodered.org)
![NPM version](https://badge.fury.io/js/node-red-dashboard.svg)
![NPM](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/node-red-dashboard)

This module provides a set of nodes in Node-RED to quickly create a live data dashboard.

These nodes require node.js version 8. The last version to support node v6 was 2.9.5.

From version 2.10.0 you can create and install widget nodes like other Node-RED nodes.
See the [Wiki](https://github.com/node-red/node-red-dashboard/wiki/Creating-New-Dashboard-Widgets) for more information.

For the latest updates see the [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/node-red/node-red-dashboard/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md)

![Dashboard example](http://nodered.org/images/dashboarde.png)

## Pre-requisites

The Node-RED-Dashboard requires [Node-RED](https://nodered.org) to be installed.

## Install

To install the stable version use the `Menu - Manage palette` option and search for `node-red-dashboard`, or run the following command in your Node-RED user directory - typically `~/.node-red`:

    npm i node-red-dashboard

Restart your Node-RED instance and you should have UI nodes available in the palette and a new `dashboard` tab in the
right side panel. The UI interface is available at <http://localhost:1880/ui> (if the default settings are used).

If you want to try the latest version from github, you can install it by

    npm i node-red/node-red-dashboard

## Settings

The default url for the dashboard is based off your existing Node-RED httpRoot path with /ui added. This can be changed in your Node-RED settings.js file - `ui: { path: "ui" },`

You can also add your own express middleware to handle requests by using the `ui: { middleware: your_function }` property in settings.js. For example

```
ui: { path: 'ui', middleware: function (req, res, next) {
            // Do something more interesting here.
            console.log('LOGGED')
            next()
        }
    },
```

You can also set the dashboard to be read only by `ui: { readOnly: true }`. This does not stop the user interacting with the dashboard but does ignore all updates coming from the dashboard.

## Layout

The dashboard layout should be considered as a grid.

Each **group** element has a width - by default 6 'units' (a unit is 48px wide by default with a 6px gap).

Each **widget** in the group also has a width - by default, 'auto' which means it will fill the width of the group it is in, but you can set it to a fixed number of units.

The layout algorithm of the dashboard always tries to place items as high and to the left as they can within their container - this applies to how groups are positioned on the page, as well as how widgets are positioned in a group.

Given a group with width 6, if you add six widgets, each with a width of 2, then they will be laid out in two rows - three widgets in each.

If you add two groups of width 6, as long as your browser window is wide enough, they will sit alongside each other. If you shrink the browser, at some point the second group will shift to be below the first, in a column.

It is advisable to use multiple groups if possible, rather than one big group, so that the page can dynamically resize on smaller screens.

## Features

#### Dashboard sidebar

The widget layout is managed by a `dashboard` tab in the sidebar of the Node-RED editor.

##### Layout

 - **Tabs** - From here you can re-order the tabs, groups and widgets, and add and edit their properties. You can also open the layout tools that may help you organise the widgets more easily than via the sidebar.

 - **Links** - to other web pages can also be added to the menu. They can optionally be opened in an iframe - if allowed by the target page.

##### Site

 - **Title** - the `title` of the UI page can be set.

# node-red-dashboard

[![platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Node--RED-red)](https://nodered.org)
![NPM version](https://badge.fury.io/js/node-red-dashboard.svg)
![NPM](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/node-red-dashboard)

This module provides a set of nodes in Node-RED to quickly create a live data dashboard.

These nodes require node.js version 8. The last version to support node v6 was 2.9.5.

From version 2.10.0 you can create and install widget nodes like other Node-RED nodes.
See the [Wiki](https://github.com/node-red/node-red-dashboard/wiki/Creating-New-Dashboard-Widgets) for more information.

For the latest updates see the [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/node-red/node-red-dashboard/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md)

![Dashboard example](http://nodered.org/images/dashboarde.png)

## Pre-requisites

The Node-RED-Dashboard requires [Node-RED](https://nodered.org) to be installed.

## Install

To install the stable version use the `Menu - Manage palette` option and search for `node-red-dashboard`, or run the following command in your Node-RED user directory - typically `~/.node-red`:

    npm i node-red-dashboard

Restart your Node-RED instance and you should have UI nodes available in the palette and a new `dashboard` tab in the
right side panel. The UI interface is available at <http://localhost:1880/ui> (if the default settings are used).

If you want to try the latest version from github, you can install it by

    npm i node-red/node-red-dashboard

## Settings

The default url for the dashboard is based off your existing Node-RED httpRoot path with /ui added. This can be changed in your Node-RED settings.js file - `ui: { path: "ui" },`

You can also add your own express middleware to handle requests by using the `ui: { middleware: your_function }` property in settings.js. For example

```
ui: { path: 'ui', middleware: function (req, res, next) {
            // Do something more interesting here.
            console.log('LOGGED')
            next()
        }
    },
```

You can also set the dashboard to be read only by `ui: { readOnly: true }`. This does not stop the user interacting with the dashboard but does ignore all updates coming from the dashboard.

## Layout

The dashboard layout should be considered as a grid.

Each **group** element has a width - by default 6 'units' (a unit is 48px wide by default with a 6px gap).

Each **widget** in the group also has a width - by default, 'auto' which means it will fill the width of the group it is in, but you can set it to a fixed number of units.

The layout algorithm of the dashboard always tries to place items as high and to the left as they can within their container - this applies to how groups are positioned on the page, as well as how widgets are positioned in a group.

Given a group with width 6, if you add six widgets, each with a width of 2, then they will be laid out in two rows - three widgets in each.

If you add two groups of width 6, as long as your browser window is wide enough, they will sit alongside each other. If you shrink the browser, at some point the second group will shift to be below the first, in a column.

It is advisable to use multiple groups if possible, rather than one big group, so that the page can dynamically resize on smaller screens.

## Features

#### Dashboard sidebar

# node-red-dashboard

[![platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Node--RED-red)](https://nodered.org)
![NPM version](https://badge.fury.io/js/node-red-dashboard.svg)

This module provides a set of nodes in Node-RED to quickly create a live data dashboard.

These nodes require node.js version 8. The last version to support node v6 was 2.9.5.

From version 2.10.0 you can create and install widget nodes like other Node-RED nodes.
See the [Wiki](https://github.com/node-red/node-red-dashboard/wiki/Creating-New-Dashboard-Widgets) for more information.

For the latest updates see the [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/node-red/node-red-dashboard/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md)

![Dashboard example](http://nodered.org/images/dashboarde.png)

## Pre-requisites

The Node-RED-Dashboard requires [Node-RED](https://nodered.org) to be installed.

## Install

To install the stable version use the `Menu - Manage palette` option and search for `node-red-dashboard`, or run the following command in your Node-RED user directory - typically `~/.node-red`:

    npm i node-red-dashboard

Restart your Node-RED instance and you should have UI nodes available in the palette and a new `dashboard` tab in the
right side panel. The UI interface is available at <http://localhost:1880/ui> (if the default settings are used).

If you want to try the latest version from github, you can install it by

    npm i node-red/node-red-dashboard

## Settings

The default url for the dashboard is based off your existing Node-RED httpRoot path with /ui added. This can be changed in your Node-RED settings.js file - `ui: { path: "ui" },`

You can also add your own express middleware to handle requests by using the `ui: { middleware: your_function }` property in settings.js. For example

```
ui: { path: 'ui', middleware: function (req, res, next) {
            // Do something more interesting here.
            console.log('LOGGED')
            next()
        }
    },
```

You can also set the dashboard to be read only by `ui: { readOnly: true }`. This does not stop the user interacting with the dashboard but does ignore all updates coming from the dashboard.

## Layout

The dashboard layout should be considered as a grid.

Each **group** element has a width - by default 6 'units' (a unit is 48px wide by default with a 6px gap).

Each **widget** in the group also has a width - by default, 'auto' which means it will fill the width of the group it is in, but you can set it to a fixed number of units.

The layout algorithm of the dashboard always tries to place items as high and to the left as they can within their container - this applies to how groups are positioned on the page, as well as how widgets are positioned in a group.

Given a group with width 6, if you add six widgets, each with a width of 2, then they will be laid out in two rows - three widgets in each.

If you add two groups of width 6, as long as your browser window is wide enough, they will sit alongside each other. If you shrink the browser, at some point the second group will shift to be below the first, in a column.

It is advisable to use multiple groups if possible, rather than one big group, so that the page can dynamically resize on smaller screens.
